title: Handling Errors: try, except and Clear Messages
concepts: why a bare except hides bugs
catching several exceptions with a tuple

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked for a load_scores() that never crashes and skips a damaged row, the AI put the whole loop inside one try block with a bare except: pass. The damaged row stopped the loop, so every row after it was lost with no message: the damaged test file gives one score instead of two. The fixed function puts a small try around each row, catches ValueError only, and gives a message for a missing file.

changes: The curriculum's 'writing helpful error messages' is taught as a rule (name the problem and the value) in Step 4 and practised in every example, rather than as a separate step.
pytest.raises is used without its match argument, to keep the chapter short; the lesson tests only the exception type.
Catching several exceptions with a tuple, except (ValueError, TypeError), appears only in the AI section, where a short row makes int() receive None.
The ask-again loop uses else and break instead of continue, because continue has not been taught.
Data files for the examples (week.csv, scores.csv and the case_*.csv test files) sit beside the examples; the checker runs every example on a fresh copy of its folder.
outstanding_issues: On a learner's computer, the error reports show the full path to the file instead of the short file name.
pytest's separator lines are wider on a learner's terminal than the 56-column reports in the lesson.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
